lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: accessibility and contingency planning

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic accessibility and contingency planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The Hollow Line Route 4 bus from the earlier Cedar Hollow errand plan is announced fictionally closed for construction this morning.

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Name one other realistic contingency, besides a route closure, that could disrupt a real trip plan, such as a schedule delay or a mobility need requiring a different stop, and explain in general terms what a person could do to prepare for that kind of disruption ahead of time.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer. | Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner plan a third contingency for the same fictional errand, this time assuming no bus is running at all that morning, and describe a full alternative plan using only walking and time estimates.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic accessibility and contingency planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: pencil
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The Hollow Line Route 4 bus from the earlier Cedar Hollow errand plan is announced fictionally closed for construction this morning.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact accessibility and contingency planning decision or action.
Model move 2: Recall or reread the original fictional plan before changing anything.
Model move 3: Read the new contingency and identify what specifically breaks in the old plan.

Model check: Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer. | Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for accessibility and contingency planning.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The Hollow Line Route 4 bus from the earlier Cedar Hollow errand plan is announced fictionally closed for construction this morning.
Coach direction: Recall or reread the original fictional plan before changing anything.
Learner prompt: In one or two sentences, restate the original Cedar Hollow plan: which bus was going to be caught and what time the errand-runner planned to leave home.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read the new contingency and identify what specifically breaks in the old plan. This morning, Hollow Line Route 4 is closed for construction between 9:00 a.m. and 11:30 a.m. A replacement route, Route 4A, runs from the Elm Street stop, a 12-minute walk from home, at 9:20 and 9:50, taking 20 minutes to reach Riverside Market.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I identified that Route 4 will not run in time for the original plan today.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Using the Route 4A details above, what time would the errand-runner need to leave home to catch the 9:20 departure from the Elm Street stop?
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Name one other realistic contingency, besides a route closure, that could disrupt a real trip plan, such as a schedule delay or a mobility need requiring a different stop, and explain in general terms what a person could do to prepare for that kind of disruption ahead of time.

Success checks: Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer. | Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional accessibility and contingency planning condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer. | Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

resources.title: accessibility and contingency planning delivered plan
resources.purpose: Resolves the lesson's named plan so the learner is never directed to a phantom material.
content: Starting information: The Hollow Line Route 4 bus from the earlier Cedar Hollow errand plan is announced fictionally closed for construction this morning.
Use steps: Read the new contingency and identify what specifically breaks in the old plan.
Field 1 (t2-p1): I identified that Route 4 will not run in time for the original plan today.
Field 2 (t2-p2): Using the Route 4A details above, what time would the errand-runner need to leave home to catch the 9:20 departure from the Elm Street stop?

Check against: Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer. | Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The Hollow Line Route 4 bus from the earlier Cedar Hollow errand plan is announced fictionally closed for construction this morning.

Give feedback against one observable success check.

simulationRoute.title: accessibility and contingency planning — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the accessibility and contingency planning task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Name one other realistic contingency, besides a route closure, that could disrupt a real trip plan, such as a schedule delay or a mobility need requiring a different stop, and explain in general terms what a person could do to prepare for that kind of disruption ahead of time.
observableCriteria: Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer.
Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Contingency identification and backup plan accuracy: Revised plan correctly uses Route 4A with an accurate leave-home time, walk and ride duration, arrival time, and closing-time buffer. | Justification and reasoning for the revised plan: Explains clearly why the revised plan still meets the booth's closing time, directly referencing the changed stop, departure, or travel time.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u04-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
